name: RESCUE BT2
fullName: Tirofiban for Stroke without Large or Medium-Sized Vessel Occlusion
population: n=1177, adults, NIHSS NIHSS ≥5 with at least one moderately-to-severely weak limb, four entry routes: ≤24 h and ineligible for reperfusion; progression at 24-96 h; early deterioration after thrombolysis; or no improvement 4-24 h after thrombolysis
teachingPoint: IV tirofiban improved 90-day excellent outcome in non-occlusive, often progressive stroke, with inconsistent secondary endpoints.

name: ATTRACTION
fullName: Adjunct Tirofiban Treatment after Successful Endovascular Thrombectomy Recanalisation in Acute Anterior Circulation Ischaemic Stroke
population: n=1380, median 71 y (IQR 62-77); 591 (43%) female, 789 (57%) male, NIHSS not restricted by a protocol NIHSS band (anterior-circulation LVO), Randomization after successful reperfusion by thrombectomy
teachingPoint: Reopens the adjunctive-antiplatelet question specifically for the post-reperfusion window, while the numerically higher symptomatic haemorrhage and the near-uniformly Han Chinese cohort mean it is not yet a general recommendation.

name: RESCUE BT
fullName: Effect of Intravenous Tirofiban vs Placebo Before Endovascular Thrombectomy on Functional Outcomes in Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke
population: n=948, mean 67 y; 391 (41.2%) women, NIHSS not restricted by a protocol NIHSS band (proximal intracranial LVO), ≤24 h from time last known well
finding: DID NOT meet superiority — neutral: median (IQR) 90-day mRS 3 (1-4) with tirofiban vs 3 (1-4) with placebo
teachingPoint: Does not support giving intravenous tirofiban before endovascular thrombectomy: 90-day disability was unchanged and symptomatic hemorrhage was numerically higher.

name: MOST
fullName: Multi-arm Optimization of Stroke Thrombolysis: Adjunctive Intravenous Argatroban or Eptifibatide for Ischemic Stroke
population: n=514, adults ≥18 y, NIHSS NIHSS ≥6 before intravenous thrombolysis, IV thrombolysis within 3 h of onset; study drug started within 75 min of the start of thrombolysis
finding: DID NOT meet superiority for either adjunct — mean (±SD) utility-weighted 90-day mRS 5.2±3.7 with argatroban, 6.3±3.2 with eptifibatide and 6.8±3.0 with placebo; both adjuncts were numerically WORSE than placebo
teachingPoint: Argues against adding intravenous argatroban or eptifibatide to IV thrombolysis in the first hours after treatment: no reduction in disability, and a numerical mortality excess the trial was stopped too early to characterise.
